reason: The mission provides over 20 verifiable claims across seven sites, including technical anomalies, political highlights, and record-breaking geriatric science.
story: Thirty-six years after becoming the first American to orbit Earth, John Glenn made history again. In 1998, at age 77, the legendary astronaut returned to space aboard the Shuttle Discovery. While some dismissed it as a publicity stunt, Glenn lobbied for years to serve as a medical "guinea pig." Scientists used the flight to study how spaceflight mimics the aging process, monitoring Glenn's bone density and sleep patterns. The mission, STS-95, was a massive event; President Bill Clinton even watched the launch from the control center roof. The flight faced immediate drama when a drag chute door fell off the orbiter during ignition, meaning Discovery had to land without it. Over nine days, Glenn completed 134 orbits, bridging the gap between the pioneer Mercury era and the Shuttle program. He remains the oldest person ever to reach Earth orbit, proving that the spirit of exploration has no expiration date.
angle: John Glenn returned to space at 77 years old, exactly 36 years after his first historic orbit, to serve as a medical guinea pig for aging research.

claims.claim: John Glenn was 77 years old when he launched on STS-95
The mission launched on October 29, 1998
The orbiter used for the mission was Discovery
The flight took place 36 years after Glenn's first orbital mission
At the time, Glenn became the oldest person to ever travel into space
Glenn remains the oldest person to ever reach Earth orbit
President Bill Clinton witnessed the launch in person
Pedro Duque became the first Spaniard in space during this mission
The crew completed 134 orbits around the Earth
The drag chute compartment door fell off the shuttle during main engine ignition
The mission carried a slate of more than 80 science experiments
The Spartan solar satellite was deployed and retrieved using the shuttle's robotic arm
The Spacehab module provided additional pressurized workspace for the experiments
Glenn was a sitting U.S. Senator from Ohio at the time of the flight
The mission tested hardware for the Hubble Space Telescope via the HOST platform
Glenn's 1962 flight was aboard the Friendship 7 capsule
Research focused on how spaceflight mimics the aging process, including bone loss and sleep disturbances
John Glenn was the only Mercury 7 astronaut to fly on the Space Shuttle
The mission released a small communications satellite called PANSAT
Glenn provided 17 blood and 48 urine samples for medical research during the mission

disputed: Mission duration is reported as 9 days, 19 hours by NASA [S2] but as 8 days, 21 hours by ESA [S3]; the script should use 'about nine days'.
Whether Glenn was truly the 'oldest person in space' depends on the definition of space; his orbital record was surpassed in age by suborbital fliers Wally Funk and William Shatner [S1, S4].

The reason Glenn did not fly again immediately after 1962 is attributed to a rumor that President Kennedy did not want to risk a national hero [S6]; the script should attribute this as 'according to one account'.
